tools.name: readiness_get_verification_token
tools.description: Step 1 of a readiness scan. Returns the domain-ownership token for the URL's host plus the three ways to publish it (DNS TXT record, <meta> tag, /.well-known file). The token is deterministic for the host, so calling this again returns the same value. Nothing is stored.

tools.name: readiness_request_scan
tools.description: Step 2. Verifies domain ownership (DNS TXT / meta tag / .well-known must carry the token from readiness_get_verification_token), then queues a Playwright probe that tries to sign up, accept the terms and mint an API key with no human. Returns the scan id and the public results URL. Fails with DOMAIN

tools.name: readiness_get_scan
tools.description: Step 3. Poll a scan by id. While status is queued/running only metadata is returned; when done you get the 0-100 score, grade, per-item rubric points with evidence, the fix list, and what could not be observed.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: readiness_get_verification_token · Private data: readiness_get_verification_token, readiness_request_scan · Public sink: readiness_get_verification_token.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: readiness_get_verification_token · Private data: readiness_get_verification_token, readiness_request_scan · Public sink: readiness_get_verification_token

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
